national_news.title: PM Modi Addresses Khelo India Dialogue Organised by MY Bharat
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the nationwide Khelo India Dialogue via video conferencing, organized by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) as part of National Sports Day celebrations across two colleges in every district.

The Prime Minister reiterated the government's commitment to creating a modern sports ecosystem, emphasizing a talent hunt initiative targeting children aged 5 to 15 years to identify their natural athletic aptitudes.
Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya highlighted key sports reforms including the National Sports Governance Act, Fit India Movement, and 'Sunday on Cycle' fitness drives.

national_news.title: Severe Flash Floods in Nepal Trigger Humanitarian Assistance from India
bullets: A massive flash flood originating in Tibet devastated central Nepal along the Lhende and Bhote Koshi rivers into the Trishuli River, triggered by an earthquake and glacial outburst near the Nepal-Tibet border.
The flood damaged 13 operational and under-construction hydropower projects with a combined capacity of 354 MW and destroyed 19 motorable bridges across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

India extended immediate humanitarian aid and relief supplies to Nepal, while the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu set up emergency helplines to assist missing Indian nationals and Kailash Manasarovar pilgrims.

national_news.title: Centre Initiates Calibrated Buffer Stock Release of Onions under PSF
bullets: The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution launched calibrated releases from buffer stock to moderate seasonal onion price volatility, supported by an estimated 2025-26 production of over 307 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT).
The government set a procurement target of 2 LMT Rabi onion for the Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) buffer for 2026-27, with 1.21 LMT already procured since May 15.
Buffer stock onions are being retailed at Rs 35 per kg through NCCF, NAFED, Safal, and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, alongside bulk rail transit via the 'Kanda Express' from Nashik to Delhi NCR.

national_news.title: Northeast Power Ministers Seek Central Funds for Grid Modernisation and PSDF
bullets: Ministers of the North Eastern Regional Power Committee (NERPC), led by Meghalaya Power Minister Metbah Lyngdoh, urged Union Power Minister Manohar Lal Khattar to provide central funds for modernising the regional power grid.

States requested targeted support under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF) and a larger allocation from the 10% Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) reserved for the Northeast across central ministries.

Priority projects discussed include SCADA/EMS systems, Emergency Restoration Systems (ERS), smart meter check systems, and additional substations to overcome challenging terrain and transmission losses.

national_news.title: Flash Floods Hit Nepal's Bhote Koshi River Affecting Kailash Manasarovar Pilgrims
bullets: Severe flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's Rasuwa region near the Tibet border, triggered by an earthquake-induced avalanche.
Over 100 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs heading for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra in Tibet were among nearly 500 missing persons.
The flood surged through Rasuwa, Dhading, Nuwakot, and Chitwan districts, damaging major bridge infrastructure across the region.

national_news.title: India Dispatches 10 Tonnes of HADR Material to Flood-Hit Nepal
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi communicated with Nepalese PM Balendra Shah, offering full support and solidarity during the flood disaster.
India dispatched 10 tonnes of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) supplies along with essential medicines to Nepal.
Top Indian leadership, including President Droupadi Murmu and EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar, pledged full assistance for relief operations.

national_news.title: India and China Hold 25th Round of Special Representatives Boundary Talks in Beijing
bullets: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi co-chaired the 25th Round of Special Representatives (SR) Talks on the Boundary Question in Beijing.
Both sides agreed on eight points of consensus, advancing negotiations based on the 2005 Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles.
Key outcomes include establishing two additional military hotline channels, two extra border meeting points, and holding the Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers.

national_news.title: Onam Harvest Festival Celebrated Across Kerala
bullets: Onam is the major harvest festival of Kerala, celebrated to mark the arrival of the new harvest season and welcome the legendary King Mahabali.
Key cultural traditions of the festival include Ona Pookkalam (floral carpets), Ona Sadya (traditional feast), Vallam Kali (snake boat races), and traditional folk dances.
Special prayers and rituals were conducted across major temples in the state, including Sabarimala, Aranmula, and Guruvayur.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Announces Women-Only University and Balika PhD Fellowship
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the setting up of an all-women 'Mahila Vishwavidyalaya' where faculty, staff, and students will exclusively be women.
Disbursed ₹600 crore via Direct Benefit Transfer under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, alongside setting a target to install solar panels for 10 lakh JEEViKA Didis by March 31.
Introduced the Chief Minister Balika PhD Fellowship providing ₹10,000 per month for four years to around 1,000 female research students to boost higher education.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Becomes First State to Achieve 50 Lakh 'Lakhpati Didis'
bullets: Bihar became the first state in India to cross the milestone of 50 lakh women becoming 'Lakhpati Didis' through state-supported livelihood programs.
Under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana, financial assistance was distributed to 1.81 crore women, with 3 lakh Jeevika Didis earning over ₹2 lakh annually.
CM Samrat Choudhary announced plans for a dedicated tracking mechanism for Lakhpati Didis and laid the foundation stone for a G+6 science block at Magadh Mahila College, Patna.

bihar_news.title: Impact Assessment of Bihar's Dedicated 'Pink Bus' Service for Women
bullets: The 'Pink Bus' service, announced in the Bihar State Budget 2025-26, offers safe and affordable mobility for women across Patna, Muzaffarpur, and Gaya with fares from ₹6 to ₹25.
An impact survey by MicroSave Consulting revealed that the service reduced daily travel costs for women by 28% to 35% compared to autos and e-rickshaws.
The service promotes inclusive employment by hiring female bus conductors, with 78% of total bus trips utilized for education and work participation.

bihar_news.title: UP-Bihar Border Villages on Alert Following Nepal Floods
bullets: Flash floods in Nepal triggered high alerts across the Uttar Pradesh-Bihar border, particularly affecting Kushinagar district.
Heavy rainwater accumulation and overflowing small drains disrupted connectivity, halting small vehicle movement and forcing reliance on tractor-trolleys.
Local administrations issued loudspeaker warnings for residents in border villages like Shivpur, Basantpur, and Marchahwa to move belongings and livestock to higher ground.

bihar_news.title: Nepal Flash Floods Raise Alarm in Bihar via Trishuli-Narayani-Gandak River System
bullets: A deadly flash flood, suspected to be a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) near the Nepal-China border, impacted Nepal's Rasuwa district.
The Central Water Commission (CWC) tracked a sudden surge in the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi rivers, moving downstream into the Gandak river system affecting Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
The disaster caused severe casualties and trapped hundreds of Indian tourists, prompting coordinated disaster monitoring across Himalayan river basins.

bihar_news.title: PMFME Bazaar Showcases Grassroots Enterprises including Bihar's Makhana Innovations
bullets: The Ministry of Food Processing Industries organized the PMFME Bazaar at the India Habitat Centre on August 24-25, featuring exhibitors from 25 States and UTs.
Launched on June 29, 2020, the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme provides a credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% up to Rs 10 lakh per unit.
Bihar's indigenous makhana was prominently showcased through value-added products like makhana-infused cookies developed by enterprises utilizing PMFME financial and technical support.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Announces Solar Energy Initiative for Jeevika Didis on Raksha Bandhan
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced a special Raksha Bandhan initiative to connect nearly 10 lakh Jeevika Didis' homes to solar energy.
Solar panels will be installed at their homes under the Prime Minister Surya Ghar scheme to reduce electricity expenses and generate additional income.
The move aims to promote clean energy, self-reliance, and sustainable livelihoods for women self-help group members in the state.

bihar_news.title: Gandak River Flood Threat Prompts Precautionary Measures in UP-Bihar Border Districts
bullets: The Central Water Commission (CWC) issued an alert for the Gandak river system following severe upstream flooding in Nepal's Trishuli river.
Authorities in Bihar opened all 36 gates of the Valmikinagar Barrage in West Champaran as a precautionary measure to manage the flood surge.
The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) deployed 20 teams across the region, placing 9 teams in Bihar and 11 in Uttar Pradesh.

bihar_news.title: GLOF Event at Tibet-Nepal Border Prompts NDRF Alert in Bihar and UP
bullets: A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) near the Tibet-Nepal border led to a sudden surge in the Trishuli River, threatening downstream areas along the Gandak River basin.
The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) positioned 9 teams in Bihar (including West Champaran and Muzaffarpur) and 11 teams in Uttar Pradesh for flood rescue operations.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Central Water Commission (CWC) are actively monitoring the downstream movement of floodwaters near the India-Nepal border.

bihar_news.title: MoSPI Reports ₹3.40 Lakh Crore Cumulative Cost Overrun in 1,775 Central Infrastructure Projects
bullets: According to a report by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) for July 2026, 1,775 ongoing central infrastructure projects (worth over ₹150 crore each) incurred a total cost overrun of ₹3,40,504 crore.

The cumulative revised cost for these monitored projects reached ₹37,10,642 crore against an original estimate of ₹33,70,138 crore, with total expenditure standing at ₹19.26 lakh crore (51.91% of revised cost).

The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the largest share with 993 projects (56% of total) worth ₹9.62 lakh crore, followed by the Ministry of Railways with 190 projects worth ₹6.38 lakh crore.
